title: German invasion of Poland
summary: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939; the battleship Schleswig-Holstein opened fire at 4:43 a.m. and Wielun was flattened that day. Britain and France declared war on 3 September, and the Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September. Germany and the USSR partitioned Poland, and the last organised Polish resistance ended on 6 October. The National WWII Museum cites over 20,000 Warsaw civilians killed.

uncertainty.note: The USHMM dates the Warsaw surrender to 28 September; the National WWII Museum gives 27 September.

as_recorded.value: In the gray morning light of September 1, 1939
The last resistance of Polish units ended on October 6.

where.modern_name: Westerplatte, Gdansk, Poland (site of the opening attack; the campaign covered all of Poland)
where.historical_name: Westerplatte, Free City of Danzig area, Poland (opening attack; the campaign covered the whole Second Polish Republic)

importance.justification: Opened the Second World War in Europe.

audience_note: Describes aerial bombing of towns, civilian deaths and mass killing.
reviewer_note: The National WWII Museum puts the Westerplatte attack at the start; the pin marks that opening attack, not the whole campaign. Warsaw surrender date differs (27 vs 28 September) so it is left out of the summary. Does not claim a link between the firing and Westerplatte beyond the museum's wording.
